title: Calibrating the 0-10 Suspiciousness Scale: Do Monitors Mean the Same Thing?

original_idea.body: Have 4-5 open monitors assign 0-10 suspiciousness to ground-truth-labeled trajectories, compare distributions and reliability diagrams, quantify miscalibration with ECE, and show how a naive shared threshold misfires.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Cross-model suspiciousness-scale miscalibration breaks fixed-threshold protocols and a recalibration recipe is directly actionable.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Have 4-5 monitors score trajectories, compute ECE/reliability diagrams; accessible, uses existing data.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped calibration audit with clear metrics.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public models/data, immediately useful recalibration recipe, lab-independent.

novelty.reasoning: Judge calibration studied; cross-model suspiciousness-scale audit for control may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Calibration studied; cross-monitor scale audit for control protocols may be open.
